extracted.intended_audience: general female readers seeking guidance on social conduct (Victorian-era etiquette/advice)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of moral and practical rules about polite social behavior, self-discipline, patience, and conversational strategy aimed primarily at women living in social/domestic contexts. Covers judgement, temper, toleration of differences, speech, and expectations in marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceal or soften personal defects
rubrics_metrics.description: One way to render less obtrusive an inharmonious color, if we possess such, is to keep it out of a strong light that will attract all eyes to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be proud of personal defects and peculiarities; minimize attention to them rather than boast. Practical tip: avoid situations (strong light / prominent contexts) that highlight the defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid boasting about faults; practice self-control
rubrics_metrics.description: When a woman boasts that she 'knows she is often impatient, but she simply cannot help it,' she acknowledges a weakness of which she should be ashamed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If undisciplined, stay apart until you learn self-control. Boasting of defects is improper; responsibility and training are expected to overcome habitual faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerate differing characters and views
rubrics_metrics.description: It is quite possible for human beings to hold contrary views from those entertained by you and me, and still be excellent members of society and reputable Christians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not demand that others 'go well together' with you; recognize that environment and education shape people and that someone uncongenial to you may be attractive in other surroundings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give others the justice of seeing their good traits
rubrics_metrics.description: We may do others the justice of seeing their good traits as well as the bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You need not like everybody, but actively look for and acknowledge pleasant qualities; sometimes acquaintances seem dull because we don't try to discover what is in them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check selfishness that leads to boredom
rubrics_metrics.description: Some people are always bored. May it not be because they look at everything animate and inanimate from a selfish standpoint, with the query in their minds, 'How does that affect me?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you feel bored or uninterested, examine whether the cause is your own selfish perspective; consider whether the other might become interesting if conversation is turned to topics that engage them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be agreeable to secure goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewed from a selfish and politic standpoint, it is to our interest to make the best of everybody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since we cannot always choose associates, look at others' pleasant sides and make yourself agreeable to insure friendly feeling; practical self-interest supports courteous behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid those who provoke strong physical repugnance
rubrics_metrics.description: When from the first there is—not a feeling of dislike, but a strong, uncontrollable personal antipathy... avoid him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's acceptable to avoid people who instinctively repel you, but you need not broadcast your impression since others may not be affected the same way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze causes of dislike; often wounded self-esteem is root
rubrics_metrics.description: Oftener some slight to ourselves, some one unfortunate speech, biases our judgment... we should often find that wounded self-esteem was the root of the evil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect on whether personal pride or a trivial spark has engendered antipathy; strive to quench the spark before it ignites into lasting enmity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise patience before responding in anger ('bide a wee')
rubrics_metrics.description: Patience has had her perfect work... the letter was deliberately torn into strips... I had concluded to 'abide a wee.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send angry letters or respond immediately in anger; let correspondence ‘cool over night’ and reconsider. Anecdote: tearing up a draft and waiting prevented impropriety and maintained composure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay judgment and weigh prior character and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In a court of justice previous character counts for much... A single equivocal circumstance... outbalances the plea of memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before concluding someone false or unworthy, consider their long record and seek explanation; do not let one rumor or half-heard word outweigh years of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret trials as discipline and practice patience under adversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing that He lets fall upon us can be 'against' us! In His hottest fires we have but to 'hold still' and bide His good time...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a theological/stoical perspective: accept disappointments as part of divine discipline and exercise patience to see mercy and purpose over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow others' ignorance; avoid compulsive correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The hardest task ever set for mortal endeavor is for us to allow other people to know less than we know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insist on forcing truth upon others; historic examples show persecution and social discord arise from refusal to tolerate error. Practically, abstain from correcting where it causes more harm than good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not waste effort disputing with self-satisfied fools
rubrics_metrics.description: To dispute with [fools] is to strengthen the stakes, and twist harder the cords of his belief in himself... the opposition consequent upon the universal desire to set other people right, the breath that blows the flame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize fools who are 'wise in their own conceit' and avoid arguing with them, since it often only entrenches their error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt conversational strategy when dealing with limited intellects
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy and politeness harmonize in the effort to meet such intellects upon what they shall not suspect is 'made ground.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply gentleness and appropriate tactics rather than blunt statements when addressing those unready or unable to grasp counter-arguments; anecdote: attempting to reason Norah was futile and bruising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize time and energy on hopeful, profitable matters
rubrics_metrics.description: If we give the fool the benefit of his license; and expend thought and care upon that which is hopeful and profitable--do we not prove ourselves prudent economists of time and labor?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many mistakes hurt only the maker; do not expend scarce resources correcting trivial or incurable errors—focus on constructive pursuits instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer kind speech; speak truth in love, not in temper
rubrics_metrics.description: It is time that people comprehended that it is not their duty to be disagreeably frank, when another's comfort is the price thereof... 'speak the truth in love!' In 'love,' recollect,--not in temper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose to encourage and console rather than to wound; truthful remarks should be delivered kindly and gently to be effective and humane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unkind, unnecessary criticism; it causes lasting harm
rubrics_metrics.description: An unkind sentence has the power of lodgment in the mind... I have never forgotten a speech which was addressed to me over twenty years ago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that gratuitous harsh remarks can scar and persist; prefer praise or neutral observation over needless sarcasm or insult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express gratitude and praise freely
rubrics_metrics.description: One such woman never forgot to thank anyone for the slightest favor... I have seen a burly policeman smile with unexpected pleasure at receiving the sweet-faced 'thank you!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small acknowledgements of kindness brighten others' days; be liberal in thanking and praising to foster goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have realistic expectations of marriage; cultivate love, patience, and tact
rubrics_metrics.description: Marriage does not change man or woman... If John is an honest gentleman who loves Mary, the chances for her happiness depend upon her common-sense and her love for John.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect transformation by marriage; prepare for trials and rely on abundant love, divine patience, and woman's tact to enable peaceful married life.
